_note: Comparison view settings. Scenario = one site + one date/time (UTC). Elevation scale steps: the shared vertical scale of the horizon panoramas is the smallest step that fits every shown Sun/Earth elevation.
_note_default_scenarios: Default pair (P4v): the two cards must differ in at least one answer. Rule: the first card stays IM-2 at 2026-11-14 00:00 UTC; the other south polar terrain site (IM-1) at the same time gives the same two answers (Sun no, Earth yes), so the second card is the same site two days later (Sun yes, Earth yes). Unit test: tests/defaults.test.mjs.
_note_timeline: Timeline (item g): span shown per card in Earth days (one lunar day, synodic month ≈ 29.53 days); Play advances the card time by play_step_minutes every play_interval_ms (hidden when the user prefers reduced motion). One year (item d): the whole table (hourly steps); lines drawn through every line_every_steps-th row (bars use every row); Play advances by year.play_step_minutes; the caption counts hours with any part of the disc (radius disc_radius_deg, same as config/pgda.json) above the horizon used.
_note_first_screen: First screen: the near-horizon strip under the panorama on terrain sites shows ±near_horizon_deg around the horizon (polar Sun/Earth angles are small). On the first card the small-shifts block starts open, and the 2D map block starts open when the window is at least map_open_min_width_px wide.
_note_sequence: Sequential comparison (challenge text: "side-by-side or sequential comparison of multiple sites"): each card has previous/next site buttons (date kept; order = the site list) and earlier/later buttons that move the time by button_step_hours (site kept). "If the date moves" lists the same two answers for the chosen time and table_steps more rows, table_step_hours apart; it starts open on the first card (first_card.sequence_open).
_note_windows: Mission window finder (SI suggestion chosen by the author, 15 Nov): "Next windows" lists stretches of the hourly table, from the chosen time on, where the Sun and Earth are both above the horizon used (centre of the disc, horizon_threshold_deg) without a break for at least the chosen length (min_hours_options, default_min_hours); at most max_listed windows. Open on the first card only (first_card.windows_open).
_note_share: Shareable link (SI suggestion chosen by the author, 15 Nov): "Copy link" puts the cards in the address as repeated param values, fields joined by separator (site id, then UTC time; own coordinates: "custom", latitude, east longitude, time). Opening such a link restores the cards; values that cannot be read are skipped with a visible notice (no readable value = default scenarios). "Now" sets every card to the current UTC time rounded down to now_step_minutes, only inside the data range (config/ephemeris.json start/stop).
_note_example: One button above the cards (P4p, guided tour reduced to one button by the independent review, 15 Nov): replaces the cards with this one scenario (the one-kilometre case of the README, deck and teachers' page) and scrolls to its Earth view. Same scenario as config/teach.json step km.
_note_example_narrow: On windows at most example_below_answers_max_width_px wide the button sits right under the first card's two answers instead of above the cards: five buttons need three rows on a phone, and the first answer must start inside the iPhone 13 first screen (ADR 0033).
